resources.string: Qualitative illustration of a normal muscle, tendon, and bone. Crimp and motion are exaggerated; anatomy and timing are not to scale. No patient measurements or calculated forces are shown.
The tendon links skeletal muscle to bone. Its collagen bundles run mostly lengthwise and have a gentle waviness called crimp at low load.
The muscle contracts and pulls on the tendon. Tension rises along the tendon, which begins to lengthen slightly.
As the tendon stretches under tension, the aligned collagen bundles become less wavy. The magnified view exaggerates this change.
The loaded tendon transmits the muscle pull to its attachment on bone. The arrow shows the direction of the pull, not the direction of bone movement.
As tension falls, elastic recoil returns the tendon toward its resting length and the crimp becomes more visible again. The tendon does not actively contract.
Crimp morphology in relaxed and stretched rat Achilles tendon
Quantifying mechanical loading and elastic strain energy of the human Achilles tendon during walking and running
